title: Work Map recovery runner-allocation and explicit-dispatch boundary

phases.objective: Register the governed Work Map Recovery dispatcher by deferring report-directory initialization until after GitHub allocates the runner and exposing repository mutation only through an explicitly dispatched tool, without weakening exact-head authorization, marker consumption, or mutation boundaries.

e2e_journeys.actor: Recovery Bootstrap and explicitly dispatched governed Work Map Recovery tool
e2e_journeys.entrypoint: Workflow dispatch with typed RECOVER_SPEC_KIT_WORK_MAP_AUTOFIX confirmation
e2e_journeys.terminal_outcome: The workflow is registrable, initializes REPORT_DIR from RUNNER_TEMP after runner allocation, accepts no pull-request or issue-comment trigger, validates an exact current pull-request head, consumes one authorization marker, and delegates only to the sole governed Work Map writer.
steps: Receive an explicit workflow dispatch from the independently governed Bootstrap surface.
Require the exact typed Recovery confirmation and pull-request number input.
Allocate the Ubuntu runner before resolving a temporary report path.
Initialize REPORT_DIR from RUNNER_TEMP and publish it through GITHUB_ENV.
Resolve the open same-repository pull request and require behind_by=0.
Consume the one-time Work Map authorization marker.
Enable and dispatch only the governed writer and integration workflows.
Publish bounded no-secret recovery evidence without protected-branch mutation or force push.
assertions: No pull_request, pull_request_target, or issue_comment trigger grants the Recovery tool mutation authority.
The workflow_dispatch input requires exact typed confirmation.
Report initialization precedes exact target resolution.
The exact authorization marker remains required and is consumed once.
Stale pull-request heads fail closed before delegation.
Direct repository mutation, protected-branch mutation, force push, and secret inclusion remain false.

phases.objective: Expose registration, Bootstrap delegation, and delegated writer-run identity through canonical workflow evidence.
Prove fail-closed behavior across invalid confirmations, disabled writer workflows, stale heads, and repeated authorization attempts.
This repository workflow registration repair has no provider canary authority.
This repository workflow registration repair grants no Production or deployment authority.
